correctness.rationale: For \(T_b\), the leaf-difference and branch-standard invariant subspaces have zero root coordinate, so they contribute no root-to-child mutual-support eigenvalues. The fully symmetric quotient has characteristic polynomial \(\lambda(\lambda-b)(\lambda-(2b+1))\), and its exact root-to-child projector entries are \(1/(b(2b+1))\), \((b-1)/(b(b+1))\), and \(-2b/((b+1)(2b+1))\). Thus the mutual support is exactly \(\{0,b,2b+1\}\) with signs \(+,+,-\). Its gcd is \(1\), so the published Laplacian parity criterion gives peak transfer exactly for even \(b\), at odd multiples of \(\pi\). Summing absolute projector entries gives the claimed amplitude. The proof is uniform for all \(b\ge2\); finite exact checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an explicit open problem from the anchor paper by giving infinitely many non-star trees with Laplacian peak state transfer. It also identifies the source paper's unique ten-vertex non-star example as the first member of a clean parameter family, and gives an exact iff parity classification, peak times, and peak probability. This is a structural result rather than a routine numerical extension. Its limitation to distance-one, decaying-probability transfer is stated explicitly.
